hypothesis: Buried accommodation-zone or oblique Walker Lane faults may laterally translate magnetic marker horizons without a Quaternary surface scarp. A non-zero local cross-corridor lag between RTP and analytical magnetic-tilt gradients should be more specific than a pointwise magnetic edge.
mechanism: Bands 2, 3, and 9 form RTP and analytical magnetic tilt; eight oblique orientations compare directional gradients at 200-600 m non-zero lags, subtract the zero-lag registration control, downweight E-W/N-S survey-axis responses, and use Band 6 TC gradient quietness only as a radiometric decoupling weight.
named_non_fault_process: Unfaulted lithologic or intrusive contacts, remanent/reversed-polarity volcanic units, and GeoDAWN flight-line/tie-line leveling seams can create the same apparent magnetic phase shift.
